page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The underlying hardware architecture is x86_64, utilizing 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong results. Multi-core execution, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with read-only small block cached speeds at 534.72 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 60.22 GB/sec. Lower relative performance is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and static web serving throughput, which fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC CPU allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a balanced compute-to-resource profile for workloads requiring consistent single-core execution. The bundled NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, though the lower memory capacity relative to vCPUs limits its suitability for large in-memory databases. It is best suited for software compilation, text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight web applications rather than high-throughput static web serving or large-scale LLM inference.
